statements.text: On March 26, President Trump signed a proclamation to impose a 25% tariff on all imported automobiles and certain automobile parts to address “a critical threat to U.S. national security,” according to a White House Fact Sheet.

A new 25% tariff on imported auto parts officially took effect at 12:01 a.m. EDT on May 3.

The 10% universal tariff that starts on April 5 will apply to nearly all imported goods, including vehicles and vehicle components. This serves as a baseline rate across countries.
